paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. God was the One doing the saving, and Peter just showed up. Peter said, "who was I to hinder the work of God?" (Acts 11:17). I think that's the most honest question a person can ask when God moves somewhere they didn't plan. Peter had a vision, a nudge from the Spirit and a houseful of Gentiles with the Holy Spirit on them. He didn't have a leg to stand on if he tried to argue with God.

Now look at what the believers in Jerusalem did. They came in with a complaint, and they heard Peter out. When they did, they had "no further objections," and they glorified God (Acts 11:18). That's NOT easy, friend. Changing your mind when you were sure you were right is like pulling a tray out of the oven and finding out the whole recipe was bigger than you thought. They let what God did be bigger than what they expected, and it ended in worship.

So here's what I'd bake into your heart today. God's grace is bigger than the lines we draw, and "God has granted even the Gentiles repentance unto life" (Acts 11:18). When you see God working in a place or a person you didn't expect, don't get in the way. Ask what Peter asked, and then do what those believers did: glorify God. And hey, the story isn't over, because the Word has more to say about what God was doing.
